headline: Surprising Bruins trending toward being (cautious) buyers on trade market
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that the Bruins, first in the Atlantic at 13-4-1, look like they could be positioned to add at the trade deadline, trending toward being cautious buyers.

Our numbers say the record flatters them a little. Boston's share of expected goals (a measure of chance quality) is 50.6 percent so far this season, which is roughly an even split with opponents. At five-on-five it rises to 52 percent, a modest edge. The gap between that and 27 points in 18 games comes down to two things: BOS has scored 9.1 more goals than its chances would predict, and its goaltending has saved 15.5 more goals than an average goalie would have faced the same shots. That second figure is large, and it is the main reason the standings look the way they do.

That is why "cautious" fits. A team playing close to even on chances with goaltending this far above expectation is a contender in the standings and a coin flip underneath. If the saves normalize, the cushion shrinks quickly. Any addition worth making would need to come at forward or on the power play, which creates just 0.6 expected goals per game so far this season.
